skill.name: dependency-audit-assistant
skill.description: Audits project dependencies for known vulnerabilities, outdated packages, dependency tree issues, and license compliance concerns.
skill.summary: Audit dependencies across common package managers for security, freshness, and license risk.
skill.author: CrazyDubya

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from reference documentation or markdown command examples. The real risks are the executable helper script, predictable /tmp/licenses.json usage, and automatic installation of external license tools.

remediation.issue: The license helper script installs tools globally when they are missing.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for explicit confirmation before installing packages, or print installation instructions and exit. Prefer local project tools or isolated environments.

remediation.issue: The license helper script writes to a predictable shared temporary file.
remediation.suggestion: Use mktemp for a unique temporary file and clean it with a trap on exit.

remediation.issue: The skill recommends commands that can modify dependencies, including automatic fixes.
remediation.suggestion: Clearly separate read-only audit commands from modifying commands, and require user approval before running update or fix commands.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Global Tool Installation
semantic_findings.description: The helper script installs missing tools with npm install -g, pip install, and go install before running license checks. This can change the user environment and fetch code from external package registries without a separate confirmation step.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The install commands are explicit and run when tools are missing. The behavior is useful for setup but has real supply-chain and environment-modification impact.

content.value_statement: Dependency risks are hard to prioritize across package managers and license rules. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical audits with clear remediation steps.
actual_capabilities: Detects common package managers from lock files and manifest files.
Suggests security audit commands for npm, Yarn, pnpm, pip, Poetry, Bundler, Maven, Go, Cargo, and Composer.
Categorizes vulnerabilities by severity, affected package, CVE, available fix, and production exposure.
Checks outdated packages and separates patch, minor, and major update recommendations.
Reviews dependency licenses and flags GPL, AGPL, unlicensed, unknown, and custom license concerns.
Provides a structured dependency audit report with recommended action priority.
limitations: It depends on local package manager tools and registry data being available.
It does not replace legal review for license obligations.
It cannot prove exploitability without understanding application runtime usage.
Some suggested commands can modify dependencies if the user approves them.

use_cases.title: Pre-release dependency review
use_cases.description: Run a structured audit before shipping a release and prioritize fixes by severity and exposure.

use_cases.title: Open source license screening
use_cases.description: Identify dependencies with GPL, AGPL, unknown, or custom licenses before adding them to a product.

use_cases.title: Maintenance backlog planning
use_cases.description: Group outdated packages by patch, minor, and major update effort for safer dependency maintenance.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic dependency audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this project for dependency vulnerabilities and outdated packages. Start with read-only checks and summarize the highest priority fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Check license compliance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review dependency licenses in this project. Flag GPL, AGPL, unknown, unlicensed, and custom licenses, then suggest safe alternatives where possible.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize vulnerability remediation
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert audit output into an action plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the dependency audit results and rank fixes by severity, exploitability, production exposure, and update risk.

prompt_templates.title: Create a release readiness report
prompt_templates.prompt: Detect all package managers in this repository, audit vulnerabilities and licenses, identify risky transitive dependencies, and produce a release readiness report.

output_examples.input: Audit this Node.js project before release.
output_examples.output: A prioritized report listing critical and high vulnerabilities first, affected packages, safe upgrade paths, and commands that require approval.

output_examples.input: Check whether our dependencies are safe for a proprietary SaaS product.
output_examples.output: A license summary that separates permissive licenses from GPL, AGPL, unknown, and custom licenses, with legal-review notes.

output_examples.input: Tell me which dependency updates are safe this sprint.
output_examples.output: An update plan grouped into patch updates, minor updates, major updates, and packages that need migration research.

best_practices: Run read-only audit commands before any update or fix command.
Review production dependencies and direct dependencies before lower-risk development-only findings.
Test dependency updates in staging and keep lock files committed.
anti_patterns: Do not run force update commands without explicit user approval.
Do not treat license guidance as legal advice for commercial decisions.
Do not ignore transitive dependencies because they are not listed directly.

faq.question: Does this skill automatically fix vulnerable packages?
faq.answer: No. It can recommend fix commands, but modifying dependencies should require explicit user approval.

faq.question: Which package managers does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers common JavaScript, Python, Ruby, Java, Go, Rust, and PHP package managers.

faq.question: Can it review licenses?
faq.answer: Yes. It identifies permissive, weak copyleft, strong copyleft, unknown, and unlicensed dependency risks.

faq.question: Is it a replacement for Snyk or Dependabot?
faq.answer: No. It helps interpret audit results and plan remediation, but it relies on package tools and advisory data.

faq.question: Can it prove a CVE affects my application?
faq.answer: Not by itself. It can help assess exposure, but runtime usage and application context still need review.

faq.question: Can Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
